obligations.note: The change adds no new roles or actions to the access matrix; it reuses the existing 'manage_payees' action. The matrix and policy files are untouched.
No changes to the auditor role or access matrix; auditor remains read-only.
No changes to the it_admin role or its restrictions; it_admin still cannot approve or release payments.

The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen uses the privileged action 'manage_payees' with mfa=False, but EXC-0185 is an approved, unexpired exception (approved by risk_owner Omar Haddad, expires 2027-01-31, scoped to this exact route and component, with a compensating control) that covers this deviation.
Session and policy code are untouched; the 15-minute idle timeout is unchanged.
The new reopen_payee in store.py only updates status and closed_at; it does not touch the sealed NPI columns (account_number, routing_number, tax_id, date_of_birth).
No changes to integrations.py or transports.py; outbound TLS requirement is unaffected.
The reopen_payee service method logs only 'reopen_payee' and the payee ID via _audit; no NPI values are passed to any log call.
reopen_payee in service.py calls self._audit(actor, 'reopen_payee', f'payee:{payee_id}'), recording actor, action, target, and time as required.
No changes to audit.py or audit retention policy; the hash-chained, 7-year retention logic is untouched.

Reopening a payee sets status to 'open', so it will no longer match the closed_payees_before query used by retention purge; this is consistent with RET-1's scope (only closed payee accounts are subject to purge).
No new outbound integrations are introduced; integrations.py and asset-inventory.json are unchanged.
The new SQL in store.py ('UPDATE payees SET status = 'open', closed_at = NULL WHERE id = ?') uses a parameterized placeholder with (payee_id,); no string interpolation is used.
No changes to payments.py approval logic; maker-checker is unaffected.
Mortgage-mortgage approval limits are untouched; this change is in payments only.
Mortgage-mortgage underwriting is untouched; this change is in payments only.
No changes to payments.py or dual-control threshold; the obligation is unaffected.
No changes to payments.py release logic or store.py find_release/add_release; idempotent release is unaffected.
Ticket CHG-25599 is approved by change_manager Erik Brandt and its components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, payments.store) cover every file the diff touches.
Sofia Santos (change_approver, payments) approved the code review for the head commit; she is not the author (Mara Costa).
The code_review approval names commit 37fd4674, which is the only and head commit; there are no later commits to void it.

The CI run on the final commit (37fd4674) reports result 'failure' with 1 failure: test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails because POST /payees/{id}/reopen is privileged (manage_payees) but has mfa=False. The full test suite is not passing, which directly violates CHG-4's requirement.

The change touches security_sensitive components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.store). A security_review approval from Ines Halvorsen (security_reviewer, not the author) exists for the head commit.
No files under protected paths (controls/*, tests/controls/*, ci/*) are modified; the four changed files are all under apps/baseline-payments/payments/.
The ticket type is 'standard', not 'emergency'; CHG-7 does not apply.

EXC-0185 is approved by risk_owner Omar Haddad, scoped to MFA-1 / payments.routes, unexpired at review time (2026-10-26 vs expiry 2027-01-31), and records a compensating control (daily reconciliation report review).

ACR-0404 covers routes.py, which is modified (new route added), so that evidence lapses. However, MFA-1 is satisfied via the approved exception EXC-0185, which serves as the alternative basis of assurance; no additional control-test evidence is strictly required when an exception covers the obligation.

summary: The change adds a POST /payees/{id}/reopen route that reopens a closed payee. While the code is well-structured (parameterized SQL, audit logging, RBAC authorization, and a valid MFA exception EXC-0185), the CI run on the final commit fails: the control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa detects that the new route uses the privileged action 'manage_payees' with mfa=False and does not pass. Because CHG-4 requires the full test suite to pass on the final commit, this obligation is refuted. The change cannot be accepted until the failing control test is resolved—either by adding MFA to the route (and removing the need for the exception) or by updating the control test (which would require a control_owner approval under CHG-6) to account for the approved exception.
